bibliographic.title: Human-in-the-loop assessment with AI: implications for teacher education in Ibero-American universities
bibliographic.authors: Diana Carolina Fajardo-Ramos, Andrés Chiappe, Javier Mella-Norambuena
bibliographic.citation_apa: Fajardo-Ramos, D. C., Chiappe, A., & Mella-Norambuena, J. (2025). Human-in-the-loop assessment with AI: implications for teacher education in Ibero-American universities. Frontiers in Education, 10, 1710992. https://doi.org/10.3389/feduc.2025.1710992

methodology.method_family: scoping review with PRISMA and PPCDO eligibility scheme
methodology.sample_description: Peer-reviewed studies on AI and assessment in Ibero-American higher education identified via Scopus (2015–2025; English/Spanish/Portuguese)
methodology.technology_context: AI-enhanced assessment tools including automated/granular feedback, adaptive testing, learning-analytics-supported grading, generative item/rubric creation, LLM-assisted evaluation, and AI-supported proctoring; distinguished from pre-AI baselines

eligibility.decision_rationale: Scoping review centered on human-in-the-loop AI assessment governance in Ibero-American higher education, with explicit governance conditions (explainability, audit trails, fairness, transparency) and LLM-assisted evaluation as one AI mechanism; however, the primary phenomenon is educational assessment rather than conversational LLM systems, chatbots, or agentic conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Provided excerpts emphasize assessment governance and search-strategy mentions of LLMs/chatbots; full text should be checked for depth of conversational-AI and operational governance content beyond assessment scoring.

appraisal.notes: Clear scoping-review objective and replicable PRISMA/PPCDO protocol with documented Scopus search blocks and dual-language queries. Single-database retrieval and Ibero-American regional focus may limit generalizability. Limitations section not visible in supplied excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: Method is coherent and adequately reported for a scoping review synthesizing 76 studies, but relevance to conversational LLM governance is indirect: LLMs appear among broader AI-assessment tools and search terms rather than as the central governance object.

coding.theme: Human-in-the-loop governance for AI-enhanced educational assessment
coding.subtheme: Teacher-education competency requirements for trustworthy AI-assisted assessment
rq_alignment: human oversight and handoff in AI systems

synthesis.main_claim: Ibero-American higher education is technically ready for AI-enhanced assessment, but progress depends on professionalizing human-in-the-loop assessment paired with explainability, data stewardship, audit trails, and clearly communicated assistance limits.
synthesis.contribution: Offers a function-by-purpose taxonomy distinguishing pre-AI from AI-specific assessment mechanisms, five teacher-education competency clusters for responsible AI-involved assessment, and a decision-oriented research agenda grounded in 76 peer-reviewed studies.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting secondary evidence for human-in-the-loop oversight, audit/traceability, explainability, and fairness/transparency governance patterns in regulated education; not as central evidence on conversational LLM system governance.

evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed scoping review using PRISMA and PPCDO with 76 included studies
evidence.excerpt: This scoping review examines how artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes assessment in Ibero-American higher education
